prior_importants.description: The prose is false. ADR 0141 and commit 2a5ae63 both say the inbox does not yet treat `retired` as it treats `landed`. That reader change is follow-up task t-mw6a2pfo, and until it lands the Needs-you line stays.

`docs/conventions/naming.md` line 76 says: "`utils` | **Pure functions only.** Cannot import `service`, `manager`, `repository`, or `client`. If it needs one of those, it isn't a util." The new file imports `./git-diff.client.js` (`runGit`, `rethrowIfKilled`), `./merge-gate.service.js` (`deleteBranchAt`, `isAncestor`, `newestMerge`, `resolveCommit`) and `./session.repository.js` (`getSession`). Its functions also run git and read the database, so they are not pure. The next maintainer will either break the util contract or have to move the file.

`RetireOutcome` is an exported interface declared in a `*.service.ts` and imported by `src/cli/index.ts`, against `docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation (exported types live in `src/core/types/*.types.ts`).

findings.description: If the merge lock is lost after the retire has finished, `withMergeLock` throws `MergeLockLostError` carrying the outcome. The `retire` action passes that error straight to `refuseScrubbed`, so the operator sees only a refusal and exit 1. The `Kept pup/<id>` notice is dropped, and a re-run then only says "already retired", so the kept branch with un-relanded work is never named. `pup land` and `pup merge` print `error.result` before refusing; do the same here.

`RetireRequest.wait` is optional, and its only non-test caller, the CLI, always passes `true`, so the `0` branch of `req.wait ? MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS : 0` is reachable only from tests. Drop the field and pass `MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` every time. That removes the option, the ternary and the CLI's `wait: true` line.
